newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Axa to take over rival UAP.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Axa to take over rival UAP.

text.p: French insurers Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris said on Tuesday they were merging to create the world's second biggest insurance company.
The move by France's most profitable insurance company Axa to take over its bigger rival took markets by surprise.

"In the face of increasingly stiff glabal competition, the project will enable AXA and UAP to build a group with an unparalleled strategic position that neither insurer could achieve alone," the companies said in a statement.
"The new group will be the world's second largest insurer and number one worldwide in terms of assets under management," it said.
Though the merger, Axa will gain a hold in the German market through UAP's German subsidiary Colonia AG while also building its presence in the French market.
"Axa feels its home base is not as strong as it would like it to be," one analyst, who declined to be named, said.
It already has a strong presence outside France, notably via its Equitable Co U.S. subsidiary and National Mutual in Australia which has given it access to the Asian market.

It reported first-half 1996 net attributable profit of 1.98 billion francs ($392 million) on turnover of 87.5 billion francs, while UAP emerged from a two-billion-franc loss in 1995 to produce a first-half 1996 net attributable profit of 860 million francs.

The management board of the new company will be headed by Axa chairman Claude Bebear while Jacques Friedmann, a close political associate of President Jacques Chirac, will become head of the newly merged company's supervisory board.
Axa and UAP said Axa would offer four of its own shares plus four certificates of guaranteed value for 10 UAP shares in a merger which will form the world's second largest insurer behind Nippon Life.

The certificates of guaranteed value, which can cashed in in 1999 if Axa shares fail to reach a certain level, are an important sweetener which ensures UAP shareholders will get more than the 152 francs per share they paid at its privatisation in 1994.

Under the terms of the deal, in June 1999, if Axa shares are trading below 392.50 per share -- the equivalent of 157 francs per UAP share -- the certificates of guaranteed value will entitle the holders to a cash payment of the difference.
Based on the average trading price of UAP stock over the last three months, the deal offered shareholders an immediate global premium of 39 percent, the statement said.

"UAP shareholders are being offered a substantial premium immediately, with the chance to recover upon maturity a value which is higher than the subscription value offered under the terms of the privatisation," the statement said.

Shares in UAP, which like other French financial institutions, was hit badly by a slump in the property market, closed on Friday at 116.9 francs per share, compared to the 152 francs per share 1994 privatisation price.
Shares in Axa closed on Friday at 318.5 francs. Trading in both shares was suspended on Tuesday at the companies' request, following Monday's public holiday.
